gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 concerns whether nodal interpolation of p_1 is defined under insufficient regularity. Gold I001 concerns a malformed global dG-star seminorm whose sums range beyond the local element while the right-hand side remains local; it requires a global interpolation estimate and extension. The shared mention of an interpolant does not identify the same formula or failed obligation.

Both identify that merely L2-in-time discrete acoustic and concentration data do not support the claimed classical time regularity or the cited classical Picard–Lindelof argument. Both specifically connect this to the failure of C2 pressure/C1 concentration conclusions and propose either stronger time continuity or an a.e./Caratheodory formulation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The well-posedness theorem applies a classical finite-dimensional ODE existence argument and asserts C2 pressure and C1 concentration despite source data that are only L2 in time; continuity of the time-dependent forcing and the corresponding classical regularity are therefore unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The L2-in-time acoustic and concentration source assumptions do not justify the claimed classical C2 pressure and C1 concentration solution classes or the classical Picard–Lindelof application.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 directly identifies the L2 time regularity, explains why the ODE right-hand side need not be continuous and why C2/C1 solutions may fail, and supplies the matching a.e./Caratheodory or time-continuity repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the missing approximation requirement on the discrete initial concentration. The error splitting and Gronwall estimate retain an initial term involving I_h u_0-u_{0,h}; allowing arbitrary u_{0,h} makes the claimed O(h^q) concentration estimate false at t=0. The proposed repairs are equivalent initial-data conditions.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The concentration convergence theorem discards or fails to control the initial discrete concentration error even though u_{0,h} is unrestricted; an O(h^q) condition relating u_{0,h} to I_hu_0 (equivalently controlling u_0-u_{0,h} at the stated approximation order) is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: The arbitrary discrete initial concentration leaves an uncontrolled initial energy term, invalidating the stated O(h^{2q}) concentration estimate unless u_{0,h} approximates u_0/I_hu_0 at order h^q.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 explicitly identifies arbitrary u_{0,h}, the discarded initial error in the Gronwall step, a counterexample at t=0, and the matching approximation repair.
